approved: Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that merges two wine industry bodies into a new statutory authority called the Australian Grape and Wine Authority.
The new authority would take over the roles of the existing organisations and start operating on 1 July 2014, with no change to the levy structure or amounts that fund them.
The explanatory memorandum says the merger aims to align strategy and reduce red tape, such as removing the need for ministerial approval of annual operational plans.
Creates the Australian Grape and Wine Authority.
Transfers assets, staff and functions from the two existing bodies to the new authority.
Amends the Wine Australia Act to establish the new authority.
Amends the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act and the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act to ensure levy collection continues under the new arrangements.
Grape growers, winemakers, and the wine industry bodies being merged.

Introduced a bill creating the Australian Grape and Wine Authority from 1 July 2014 by merging the Grape and Wine Research and Development Corporation with Wine Australia, describing an industry worth approximately $3.4 billion annually, and noted Australian wine exports to China have grown from $57 million in 2007 to $250 million today.

Introduced a companion bill updating the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act 1999 to replace references to the Wine Australia Corporation with the new Australian Grape and Wine Authority, and removed the requirement for Wine Australia's annual meeting to recommend levy rate changes, aligning the wine industry's levy process with other sectors.

Introduced a second companion bill updating the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999 to replace references to the Wine Australia Corporation with the new Australian Grape and Wine Authority, and removed the requirement for Wine Australia's annual meeting to recommend levy rate changes, aligning the wine industry's levy process with other sectors.

Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill, a Labor-initiated measure merging the Grape and Wine Research and Development Corporation and Wine Australia into a single authority from 1 July 2014, and described Australia as the world's fourth largest wine-exporting country facing pressure from a high dollar and growing retail market concentration.
Referred the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013 and two related customs and excise levy bills to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill merging two wine industry bodies into the Australian Grape and Wine Authority, citing a $3.4 billion national wine industry and Hunter region exporters, and said Australian wine exports to China grew from $57 million in 2007 to more than $250 million.

Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill, noting Australia's wine exports to China grew from $57 million in 2007 to $250 million in 2013 but lag New Zealand due to the lack of a free trade agreement, and said the industry includes more than 2,500 wine producers and 6,000 grape growers.

Supported the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill but warned that supermarket duopoly control of 60 to 70 per cent of retail wine sales was squeezing producers, citing a KPMG report showing trade spend paid to retailers rose from 19.5 to 23.4 per cent of gross sales between 2008-09 and 2011-12.

Concluded debate on the Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill, confirming the merger followed an industry proposal submitted in August 2012 by Wine Grape Growers Australia and the Winemakers Federation of Australia, and said the coalition's review of the Competition and Consumer Act would examine unconscionable conduct provisions affecting small winemakers' ability to market their products.

Moved to schedule non-controversial government bills for consideration from 12:45 pm, including amendments to the Australian Civilian Corps, Import Processing Charges, Grape and Wine Authority, Offshore Petroleum, Rural Research and Development, and Customs Anti-Dumping Commission. Also moved to set general business order for the day, prioritising Senator Moore's motion on pre-election commitments and government document orders.
